description: Retrieval gold set for the fixture payloads (18 from phase 2, 19 added in phase 6) (SUPPLIER_RISK_EVIDENCE_ENGINE_PLAN.md, sections 9 and 10). Compare each fixture's returned evidence_ids with expected_ids and report missed and unexpected IDs. expected_links and expected_exclusions explain each entry; only expected_ids is the pass/fail comparison.
status: agreed 2026-11-15: derived by applying the plan's rules to the stored records, then reviewed by hand. Not produced by the engine. The interpretations were agreed with the user on 2026-11-15.

evidence_database.note: If the database changes, recheck every fixture against the new records.

payload_source: build_payloads.py, from data/processed/*_shipments_clean.csv (the graph's import files) plus supplier country and parent from the Neo4j graph.

interpretations.rule: A record is expected at most once per supplier. When several bases link it, the strongest is listed (strong > medium > weak) with every matched value.

Records are expected only when they link on their own. A related record (related_evidence_ids) that does not link is not added to the expected set; section 4 'return them together' is read as grouping linked records.

A record without its date field is expected only when as_of_date falls inside its search_window; event_window_days is not applied to search windows. Since phase 6 it must also be known by as_of_date (known_from on or before as_of_date).

The event window extends only the end of effective intervals, so a tariff ending 2025-11-09 is in scope on 2025-11-21 with a 14-day window. Revised 2026-11-15 (phase 6): it no longer extends the start.

Port tiers (port_code, port_name, port_country) apply to port_disruption, natural_hazards and border_customs_delays, using both exit and entry ports. No graph port code equals a record code because records carry no port codes.

The port_country tier also applies to natural_hazards and border_customs_delays (section 5.1 states the tiers generically). If it applies only to port_disruption, the dependent IDs listed here drop out.
port_disruption links by country only through a port's country (port_country), never through the supplier country (section 7: 'allowed as port_country').

For every other type that allows country-only links, the supplier country is compared with the record's country field; port countries and importing_country are not used, except importing_country for tariffs and trade lanes.
Graph carrier names such as 'MAEU - Maersk Line' are sent as name 'Maersk Line' and code 'MAEU'. Under exact normalised equality 'Maersk Line' does not match 'Maersk (charterer)'.
Port-name containment is applied literally, so exit port Manila links CUSTOMS-2026-PH-001 (Ninoy Aquino International Airport cargo facilities, Manila).

Tariffs need origin = supplier country and importing = request importing_country; a null origin links on importing country alone (basis importing_country); a record with a code also needs an HS prefix match.
Payloads carry the supplier's full shipment footprint, including shipments after as_of_date. The engine never filters on footprint dates.

A record is expected only from its known_from date (plan section 5.2): a stored known_from, else its start date, else source.published_at. event_window_days extends past the end only. Each expected link records known_from and known_from_rule. A record known after its end (or after its search window) stays in scope for event_window_days from known_from (late-report rule, agreed 2026-11-15).
